Fire Protection Systems
Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: FS-048-R0A
Equipment: Automatic water fire extinguishing system (Automatic wet pipe system) for the emergency diesel areas 1–2, Caterpillar 3608 DI
Issued to: Damietta Combined Cycle Power Station
Document status: Approved
Date of document approval:
Procedure: The fire system test is carried out every six months
Date of next review:

sections_en.text: This system is used to protect the emergency diesel areas 1–2. It consists of a network of sprinklers on a branch fire-water line that is always under the pressure of the main fire-water network and connected to it through an alarm check valve. This system does not rely on heat detectors for its operation; it operates through closed-type water sprinklers that fuse automatically when the temperature rises – a fusible-link type sprinkler – which is affected at 100 °C. The system is fitted with an audible alarm device (sprinkler alarm), which gives a continuous audible alarm when the fire system operates.
The system is also fitted with a retarding chamber to prevent the sprinkler alarm from operating when sudden pressure changes occur.

In the event of a fire, the high temperature causes the fire-water sprinklers to fuse, so the sprinklers open and water flows out of them directly onto the fire area. The flow of water through the fire valve (alarm valve) sends a signal to the control panel and raises a fire alarm, and also operates the audible alarm device.

This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif, reviewed by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed – Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department – and the field test was carried out by Instrumentation Maintenance Engineer Raafat Madin. It was reviewed by the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Chemist Ahmed Abdullah, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan – Head of Damietta Power Station Sector.

sections_en.text: Type: Auto – fusible link type sprinkler. Rated: 100 °C

rows: Close the main isolation valve
Open the main drain valve
Remove the valve cover bolts and lift the cover to inspect the valve parts
Clean the internal valve parts and check that the rubber diaphragm and gasket are sound
Reassemble, making sure the valve gate moves freely about its axis
Disconnect the drain pipe from the lower opening of the chamber
Remove drain plug No. 4
Remove the drain orifice No. 7, the cover 6 and the internal strainer 5
Clean all these parts thoroughly

sections_en.text: Third: Audible Alarm Device (Water Motor Alarm)

rows: Close the manual test valve (Alarm check valve)
Remove the pipe connection (plug) No. 6
Remove the cover bolts No. 2, lift the cover and gasket No. 7 off the body No. 4
Remove the impeller No. 3
Inspect the injector No. 5, clean it carefully and clear the inlet line to it
Clear the manual drain line (drain outlet) and the inlet line to the injector with water or compressed air
Clean the alarm line strainer located before the injector
Reassemble, replacing gasket No. 7
Carry out the alarm test and the flow test as follows: Alarm test
Open the alarm test valve
Make sure the pressure reading does not change before and after the valve
Water flows from the drain opening of the retarding chamber
After about half a minute the chamber and the alarm line fill with water and the fire alarm device (water motor alarm) operates
Semi-annual flow test (Flow test)
Open the main drain valve fully
Make sure the fire-water pressure reading does not change
After the retarding chamber and the alarm line fill with water, the fire alarm device operates
If the fire pressure drops, check that the isolation valves are open and that there are no obstructions in the line, and clean the strainer at the inlet of the fire system
Reset the fire system, close the main drain valve and close the test valve

Introduction
This system is used to protect the emergency diesel areas 1–2. It consists of a network of sprinklers on a branch fire-water line that is always under the pressure of the main fire-water network and connected to it through an alarm check valve. This system does not rely on heat detectors for its operation; it operates through closed-type water sprinklers that fuse automatically when the temperature rises – a fusible-link type sprinkler – which is affected at 100 °C. The system is fitted with an audible alarm device (sprinkler alarm), which gives a continuous audible alarm when the fire system operates.
The system is also fitted with a retarding chamber to prevent the sprinkler alarm from operating when sudden pressure changes occur.
How the System Works
In the event of a fire, the high temperature causes the fire-water sprinklers to fuse, so the sprinklers open and water flows out of them directly onto the fire area. The flow of water through the fire valve (alarm valve) sends a signal to the control panel and raises a fire alarm, and also operates the audible alarm device.
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif, reviewed by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed – Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department – and the field test was carried out by Instrumentation Maintenance Engineer Raafat Madin. It was reviewed by the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Chemist Ahmed Abdullah, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan – Head of Damietta Power Station Sector.

First: Water Valve (Alarm Check Valve)

Second: False-Alarm Prevention Chamber (Retarding Chamber)
Disconnect the drain pipe from the lower opening of the chamber | 
Remove drain plug No. 4 | 2
Remove the drain orifice No. 7, the cover 6 and the internal strainer 5 | 3
Clean all these parts thoroughly | 4
Third: Audible Alarm Device (Water Motor Alarm)
Close the manual test valve (Alarm check valve) | 1.
Remove the pipe connection (plug) No. 6 | 2.
Remove the cover bolts No. 2, lift the cover and gasket No. 7 off the body No. 4 | 3.
Remove the impeller No. 3 | 4.

Clear the manual drain line (drain outlet) and the inlet line to the injector with water or compressed air | 6.
Clean the alarm line strainer located before the injector | 7.
Reassemble, replacing gasket No. 7 | 8.
Carry out the alarm test and the flow test as follows: Alarm test | 
Open the alarm test valve | 1.
Make sure the pressure reading does not change before and after the valve | 2.
Water flows from the drain opening of the retarding chamber | 3.
After about half a minute the chamber and the alarm line fill with water and the fire alarm device (water motor alarm) operates | 4.
Semi-annual flow test (Flow test) | 
Open the main drain valve fully | 1.
Make sure the fire-water pressure reading does not change | 2.
After the retarding chamber and the alarm line fill with water, the fire alarm device operates | 3.
If the fire pressure drops, check that the isolation valves are open and that there are no obstructions in the line, and clean the strainer at the inlet of the fire system | 4.
Reset the fire system, close the main drain valve and close the test valve | 5.
